# Herbs Share a Balcony, Not a Watering Schedule

Basil, rosemary, and mint may sit on the same shelf while needing different containers and moisture. Treating them as one “herb box” usually leaves rosemary wet or basil wilted.

## Group by roots and exposure

Mint earns its own pot because it spreads aggressively. Rosemary needs sharp drainage and tolerates a drier interval; basil responds faster to heat and wind. Observe which side receives reflected afternoon sun, not only the hours printed on a plant label.

## Feed lightly and inspect runoff

Mature compost improves a potting mix in modest amounts, but unfinished material can tie up nutrients or attract flies. Water each container until the root zone is reached, then compare how quickly it becomes light again. Adjust one plant rather than soaking the shelf.

For diagnosing compost before it reaches a pot, see [[06-compost-moisture|Balancing Moisture in a Small Compost Bin]].
